# Compiler comparison fixture v1

The source and `gold.json` were authored and source-reviewed before examining
compiler/indexer output. They are synthetic research judgments; independent human
review remains pending. This is a semantic identity and binding contract probe,
not a complete precision benchmark or a claim of CodeGraph parity.

All six projects target `net10.0`, require no NuGet package dependencies, and use
explicit imports. App and AppFast reference Contracts. AppFast links App's exact
source files and defines `FAST`; ContextA and ContextB link the same physical
`Shared/LinkedCall.cs` while supplying different project-local `Bindings.Target`
definitions. The local target methods have the same qualified spelling and source
position but different source content and project identity.

| Project | Expected state | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Contracts | Complete | Overloads, generic method, nested generic type, interface, partial declarations, same-name types with different generic arities |
| App | Complete | Project-reference bindings, interface dispatch, supplied generated source, framework reference, default conditional branch |
| AppFast | Complete | Identical caller bytes, different conditional symbols and active overload |
| ContextA / ContextB | Complete | Identical linked caller bytes resolve to distinct project-local symbols |
| Broken | Incomplete | Unresolved receiver and genuinely ambiguous overload; errors must remain explicit |

## Gold interpretation

Every reference names a project context and a physical fixture-relative source
anchor (`file`, 1-based `line`, exact token `text`). The token occurs once on its
line. Its expected target is another project-qualified declaration anchor, an
explicit external documentation ID, or an unresolved/ambiguous/inactive status.
Source spans use UTF-8 byte offsets. App's first overload invocation includes a
non-ASCII comment before its method token to distinguish UTF-8 offsets from UTF-16
and codepoint coordinates.

- `worker.Work(9)` resolves to `IWorker.Work(int)`, not directly to the concrete
  implementation. Runtime dispatch and whole-program call graph expansion are
  outside this label.
- `Echo<string>` and `Outer<int>.Inner.Keep` map to their original source
  declarations despite constructed generic symbols.
- `Box<T>` and `Box<T, U>` must have distinct identities. Both overload `Pick`
  declarations must also remain distinct; incidental declaration order is not a
  stable semantic signature.
- Two partial `PartialWidget` declarations represent one symbol. The linked
  `LinkedCaller.Run` declarations and `Target.Resolve` methods belong to distinct
  project contexts even when short/qualified names or bytes coincide.
- Inactive branch tokens must produce no resolved reference for that context.
- `Console.WriteLine(string)` is framework-external, not unresolved. Restored
  NuGet package identities/version changes remain deferred.
- `AutoGenerated.g.cs` is checked-in supplied generated input. No actual source
  generator execution is exercised or claimed.
- Broken's missing receiver requires `CS0103`; `Choose(null)` requires `CS0121`
  and the two interface-overload candidates. Expected diagnostics are required
  minimums, not a prohibition on other compiler diagnostics.

The identity groups express equality/inequality through source anchors rather
than adopting either engine's native descriptor format. Adapters must preserve
native records and derive anchor mappings without reading gold answers. Source
and project/configuration digests should accompany every run.

The Go `LoadCompilerGoldSuite` validator checks schema shape, project membership,
source token spans, identity-group structure and explicit coverage. It does not
compile C# or prove the gold semantics. Run its hermetic checks with:

```sh
go test ./internal/eval -run '^TestCompilerGold' -count=1
```

Actual source generators, restored packages, broad framework/domain relationships,
private-corpus quality and paired CodeGraph execution require separate evidence.
